parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4 falsely asserts that |E|<|V| forces the multigraph to have no cycle/loop, so the component of vertex n is a tree; it need not be. Fix: pick any tree component (exists by counting), since (3.1) holds for all J.

errors.description: The counting claim is wrong: a multigraph with fewer edges than vertices can still contain a loop or cycle (e.g. a loop at one vertex plus isolated vertices). Concretely, for n=2 Y can cut 4u into 2u,2u; with adverse tie-breaking the pair {2u,2u} is a loop at vertex n, so the component of vertex n is not a tree. The argument only shows SOME component is a tree, which suffices because (3.1) applies to every nonempty J — but this is not what is written.
errors.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible. Hence every component of $G$ is a **simple tree**; let $T=(V_T,E_T)$ be the component containing the vertex $n$

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) with correct picking-phase reduction (Lemma 2), correct upper bound via subset-sum pigeonhole and aligned cross-cutting (Lemma 5), and a sound tree-pairing lower bound modulo the misstated graph fact. Repair is a one-line change using ingredients already present; numerical checks earn no credit.
